## What the main programs cover
### Veterinary Technician
Veterinary Technician is a new AAS, and its program page says it is “currently undergoing the accreditation process” with the AVMA’s Committee on Veterinary Technician Education and Activities; the AAS is awarded “upon program accreditation”. Applicants need a 2.8 GPA or 8 college credits at 2.0, 16 hours of animal experience and an essay. Because the program is not accredited yet, there are no VTNE pass rates; ask how accreditation status affects your eligibility for that exam.

## Tuition, cost of attendance and financial aid
Iowa Central charges one rate to all Iowa residents, whether or not they live in the college’s district. The official 2025-26 rates, from the Iowa Department of Education’s summary of the college’s budget (May 2026), were:
| Per credit hour, 2025-26 | Iowa residents | Non-residents |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Tuition and fees, including the $19 per-credit fee | $235 | $330.50 |
The tuition calculator also has a separate category for non-residents with a 3.0 GPA. For 2026-27, the college’s cost-of-attendance sheet lists $6,690 tuition plus $570 fees for a full-time, two-semester in-state year, marked “Pending Board Approval”. The same sheet estimates the full 2026-27 cost of attendance, including room, board, books and transport, at $21,839 for an Iowa student living in a residence hall and $24,704 for an out-of-state student; room and board is $9,140 and books and supplies $1,460.
Truck-driver training is priced separately: the college lists tuition as “$7,000 plus”, with on-site housing at $1,900, and says students may pay nothing upfront if they qualify for grants or financial aid. A Nurse Aide course costs $697 for credit, or $116 in materials plus a $190 state test fee as a non-credit course. The payment plan carries a $25 fee per semester, and the business office charges no late fees, interest or card fees.
Iowa Central takes federal financial aid (OPEID 00186500). Its Workforce Pell program, approved in August 2026, extends Pell grants to shorter job-training courses, and HLC approved a Pell-eligible prison education program in February 2025. Diesel students can apply for the Titan Machinery Service Technician Sponsorship.

## Open admission, selective health programs and online degrees
Admission to the college is open: anyone with a high school diploma or equivalent can take courses. Several programs choose their students, with fixed application windows where published:
*   Associate Degree Nursing and Practical Nursing: 15 October to 15 March for fall, 15 May to 15 September for spring.  
*   Dental Hygiene and Radiologic Technology: 1 November to 1 March.  
*   Diagnostic Medical Sonography: 1 November to 1 April.  
*   Medical Laboratory Technician, Medical Assistant, Dental Assisting and Emergency Medical Services: selective; ask for current dates.  
*   Veterinary Technician: 2.8 GPA or 8 college credits at 2.0, 16 hours of animal experience and an essay.
Most career programs run as daytime classes on the Fort Dodge campus; truck driving runs Monday to Friday, 8 to 4. In August 2026 the college introduced an 8-week course format. Nine associate degrees are offered online: the AA transfer degree, Accounting Associate, Business, Computer Networking Technology, Criminal Justice, Digital Arts, Health Care Administration (an Associate in Professional Studies), Human Services and Medical Laboratory Technician, which needs local clinical training.

## Accreditation and published results
Iowa Central has been accredited by the Higher Learning Commission since 1974. Its last reaffirmation was in 2020-21 and the next is due in 2030-31. In September 2025 HLC completed an Assurance Review and continued the college’s accreditation, and HLC lists no sanctions.
Program accreditation: ACEN accredits Associate Degree Nursing; CODA accredits Dental Hygiene and Dental Assisting; JRCERT accredits Radiologic Technology; NAACLS accredits Medical Laboratory Technician; and CAAHEP accredits the Medical Assistant diploma. Veterinary Technician is going through AVMA CVTEA accreditation and is not accredited yet. Fire Science certifications come through the Iowa Fire Service Training Bureau, which is IFSAC-accredited.
Published results:
| Measure | Result | Year or cohort | Source |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| NCLEX-RN, first-time candidates (Associate Degree Nursing) | 83.16% (95 tested); 91.14% | 2025; 2024 | Iowa Board of Nursing |  
| NCLEX-PN, first-time candidates (Practical Nursing) | 94.55% (110 tested) | 2025 | Iowa Board of Nursing |  
| ASCP certification exam (Medical Laboratory Technician) | 100% each year | Graduates 2022 to 2026 | Program page |  
| CMA exam (Medical Assistant) | 96.08% five-year average | 2020 to 2024 | Program’s 2025 annual report |  
| Graduation within 150% of normal time | 42% | Full-time, first-time students who started in fall 2021 | College Navigator |  
| Fall-to-fall retention | 52% full-time; 39% part-time | Fall 2023 to fall 2024 | College Navigator |
We found no published pass or placement rates for dental hygiene, dental assisting, sonography, veterinary programs or truck driving. Iowa Central enrolled 4,949 students in fall 2024.

## Before you enroll
*   Veterinary Technician is not yet accredited by the AVMA’s CVTEA; the college says the program is going through the process and awards the AAS only upon accreditation. Ask what happens to your degree and exam eligibility if accreditation is not granted by the time you finish.  
*   The NCLEX-RN first-time pass rate fell to 83.16% in 2025 from 91.14% in 2024 (Iowa Board of Nursing), while the practical nursing rate rose to 94.55%. Ask the nursing department what has changed.  
*   Storm Lake and Webster City are smaller centers. The college’s pages confirm nursing faculty, nurse aide sections and general-education courses there, but most trade and health programs are taught in Fort Dodge, so check where every course in your program meets before planning to study at a center.  
*   The Electrical Technologies route to the journeyman exam needs 6,000 hours of work after graduation, and the college says it applies only in Iowa. The apprenticeship requires a job with an Iowa-registered electrical contractor.  
*   The college’s online-learning page does not mention interstate authorization for online study, so students outside Iowa should ask whether they can enrol in its online degrees. Niche reviewers describe the 8-week online terms as intense for working students, and 42% of full-time students who started in fall 2021 graduated within three years.

## Housing, internships and employer links
Iowa Central has residence halls on the Fort Dodge main campus, and its housing page also lists East Campus; 2026-27 room and board is $9,140. Truck-driving students can rent furnished housing on site. Several programs build work experience into the credential: the Electrical Technologies 8-week summer internship, the Plumbing Technology summer internship, the Medical Assistant 30-day practicum, practicums in Culinary Arts and Baking, and the 210-hour truck-driving placement with the hiring employer. The college also announced an apprenticeship partnership with Elanco in 2026. The Storm Lake center has an Academic Resource Center.

## What students say
On Niche, Iowa Central averages 3.96 out of 5 from 440 reviews, with an overall grade of C+ (checked 9 October 2026). Reviewers most often praise friendly, helpful instructors and staff, affordable tuition, and a welcoming campus that is easy to get around. The most common complaints are the small town’s limited amenities, mixed views of dining and of dorm conduct (some mention drug use), some instructors who seem not to care, and intense 8-week online terms. The newest dated reviews are from August and September 2025, and we saw no sign of a burst of posts, but we did not compare them with another review platform.

**What is NSWERS?**
NSWERS is a partnership between Nebraska’s public education system, in affiliation with the Nebraska Department of Labor, to create a data-informed decision culture that supports successful pathways of learning and earning for the people of Nebraska. In 2020, the Nebraska Legislature codified this idea into law (LB 1160), envisioning NSWERS as a “comprehensive, sustainable, and robust lifelong learning and workforce longitudinal data system to allow for the targeting of resources and focus data analysis on assessing workforce development and employment success to enable the training of tomorrow’s workforce.
**What are the NSWERS outcomes?**
NSWERS is currently focused on eight key longitudinal outcomes –four education and four workforce-related. The data elements identified in the NSWERS File Specifications are used to operationalize these eight outcomes in addition to the research constructs used to longitudinally analyze these outcomes across Nebraska’s education-workforce continuum.
**Where can I find information about the NSWERS outcomes?**
Visit the NSWERS Outcomes page on the NSWERS website at: https://nswers.org/insights/outcomes/.
**What is insights?**
insights is NSWERS’ public platform that features public data products aligned with the NSWERS Information & Research Agenda (found on the NSWERS website at https://nswers.org/insights/information-research-agenda/). Products include dashboards, data briefs, special reports, stories and more, each highlighting NSWERS’ eight longitudinal outcomes.
**Who might be interested in the insights public portal?**
insights is a useful resource for educational institutions and workforce development agencies to design and improve educational and training programs that align with the needs of Nebraska businesses. It is also useful for individuals who are working with students or clients who are trying to determine their own career path.
**What institutions are represented in this data? Where does the data come from?**

The majority of data used in the insights public portal is drawn from the NSWERS Data System. Data includes records for Nebraska public high schools and Nebraska public postsecondary institutions. Data was not provided by Central Community College. Employment information is sourced from Nebraska’s Unemployment Insurance quarterly wage reports. Data is supplemented with other sources. For example, the NSWERS data system currently does not contain program completion data for private colleges in Nebraska. For this reason, NSWERS used the program completer counts from Nebraska private postsecondary institutions as reported to the National Center for Educational Statistics’ Integrated Postsecondary Educational Data System (IPEDS).
**How do I find out what an acronym or term means?**
Visit the Data Dictionary icon in the upper right corner.
**I need help with an issue that isn’t covered in this FAQ. What should I do?**
Please send an email to [info@nswers.org](mailto:info@nswers.org).
**Does the NSWERS Data System replace annual reporting and collection requirements?**
NSWERS serves as a clearinghouse where data are linked across partner agencies and institutions to support evaluation. NSWERS does not replace institute or agency data collection and administration responsibilities.
**What does “student type” mean? How do I change it?**
Student type refers to the population of students included in each analysis. Each outcome may focus on a different population, depending on the goal of the analysis. For example, outcomes like talent retention may analyze students two years after their educational exit, which means the cohort is determined based on when these students first enrolled or exited. To change the student type, use the dropdown menu provided on the page.
**How do I know which students are represented in the data?**
Students included in the data are typically those enrolled at Nebraska public institutions or tracked via partnerships with the National Student Clearinghouse and Nebraska Department of Labor. Additional details are available for each outcome under the data definitions tab.
**Why is the most recent year of data several years old?**
Certain outcomes, such as time to employment, require a delay to allow for the observation of long-term results. For instance, employment outcomes look at students two years after they finish their education. Additionally, there may be delays in obtaining data from partners like the National Student Clearinghouse or the Nebraska Department of Labor.
**How is the data verified for accuracy?**

When data is submitted by NSWERS partners, it undergoes validation checks for issues related to formatting, data types, and consistency. This ensures that the data adheres to predefined standards before it is integrated into the data analysis. After NSWERS calculates summary statistics, such as counts, rates, and proportions, these figures are provided back to the data partners. This step allows partners to review the calculated statistics and ensure they align with their own records, verifying the data’s accuracy and consistency. After the initial submission and certification process, ongoing cross-validation ensures that any discrepancies or errors identified are remedied.
**What do the longitudinal data buttons show, and how can I view trends over time?**
Selecting the longitudinal data button changes the figure from a single-year bar chart to a line graph, showing trends over time. This feature allows users to observe changes in outcomes across different years and demographic groups. Note that while calculation methods are consistent across years, variations in data quality may occur.

In 2024, 2,842 degrees were awarded across all undergraduate and graduate programs at Central Community College. 47.1% of these degrees were awarded to women, and 52.9% awarded men. The most common race/ethnicity group of degree recipients was white (1,932 degrees), 2.48 times more than then the next closest race/ethnicity group, hispanic or latino (778 degrees).
The median undergraduate tuition at Central Community College is $2,880, which is $−5,280 less than the national average for Associates Colleges ($8,160).

# East Central Community College
## Summary
East Central Community College is a public institution in Decatur, Mississippi. Its campus is located in a rural with a total enrollment of 2,388. The school utilizes a semester-based academic year. The student-faculty ratio is 18-to-1. The highest degree offered at East Central Community College is an associate degree. The school has an open admissions policy and offers credit for life experiences.
The in-state tuition and fees for 2020-2021 were $3,150, and out-of-state tuition and fees were $5,250. There is no application fee.
Students can earn degrees and certificates in 26 different fields. Popular programs include: Liberal Arts and Sciences, General Studies and Humanities, Other, Registered Nursing/Registered Nurse, and Child Care Provider/Assistant.

## About
In 2024, 2,842 degrees were awarded across all undergraduate and graduate programs at Central Community College. 47.1% of these degrees were awarded to women, and 52.9% awarded men. The most common race/ethnicity group of degree recipients was white (1,932 degrees), 2.48 times more than then the next closest race/ethnicity group, hispanic or latino (778 degrees).
The median undergraduate tuition at Central Community College is $2,880, which is $−5,280 less than the national average for Associates Colleges ($8,160).
texts.2:
## Costs
In 2024, the median undergraduate tuition at Central Community College is $2,880, which is $5,280 less than the national average for Associates Colleges ($8,160).
After taking grants and loans into account, the average net price for students is $7,856.
In 2024, 32% of undergraduate students attending Central Community College received financial aid through grants. Comparatively, 9% of undergraduate students received financial aid through loans.

## Enrollment
Central Community College had a total enrollment of 6,927 students in 2024. The full-time enrollment at Central Community College is 1,821 students and the part-time enrollment is 5,106. This means that 26.3% of students enrolled at Central Community College are enrolled full-time.
The enrolled student population at Central Community College, both undergraduate and graduate, is 67.7% White, 27.1% Hispanic or Latino, 2.6% Black or African American, 0.982% Asian, 0.808% American Indian or Alaska Native, 0.332% Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islanders, and 0.318% Two or More Races.
Students enrolled at Central Community College in full-time Undergraduate programs are most commonly White Female (32.3%), followed by White Male (30.5%) and Hispanic or Latino Female (16.2%).

# East Central Community College
## Summary
East Central Community College is a public institution in Decatur, Mississippi. Its campus is located in a rural with a total enrollment of 2,388. The school utilizes a semester-based academic year. The student-faculty ratio is 18-to-1. The highest degree offered at East Central Community College is an associate degree. The school has an open admissions policy and offers credit for life experiences.
The in-state tuition and fees for 2020-2021 were $3,150, and out-of-state tuition and fees were $5,250. There is no application fee.
Students can earn degrees and certificates in 26 different fields. Popular programs include: Liberal Arts and Sciences, General Studies and Humanities, Other, Registered Nursing/Registered Nurse, and Child Care Provider/Assistant.

# East Central Community College
## Summary
East Central Community College is a public institution in Decatur, Mississippi. Its campus is located in a rural with a total enrollment of 2,388. The school utilizes a semester-based academic year. The student-faculty ratio is 18-to-1. The highest degree offered at East Central Community College is an associate degree. The school has an open admissions policy and offers credit for life experiences.
The in-state tuition and fees for 2020-2021 were $3,150, and out-of-state tuition and fees were $5,250. There is no application fee.
Students can earn degrees and certificates in 26 different fields. Popular programs include: Liberal Arts and Sciences, General Studies and Humanities, Other, Registered Nursing/Registered Nurse, and Child Care Provider/Assistant.
